text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - Bunds posted one of their biggest declines of the month after a bout of profit taking following last week's gains was given added urgency by worries about the health of Russian President Boris Yeltsin. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 97.86, down 0.39 from Friday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts struggled to stay afloat but ended with smaller losses than seemed likely at one stage and outperformed Bunds along the way. Bonds posted losses across Europe amid jitters about an imminent U.S. interest rate rise. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 107-12/32, down 8/32 from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bond futures consolidated, tracking Bunds, to settle near their lows as the market waited for the outcome of Tuesday's long-awaited US FOMC gathering. One analyst said some investors had lightened their positions ahead of the meeting but that the market had been overbought. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 123.86, down 0.34 from Friday's settlement price.

ITALY - Bonds and futures closed quietly lower ahead of preliminary September inflation data from six Italian cities, with the market cautious over possible snags over the 1997 budget package. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 118.35, down 0.40 from Friday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries were in negative territory in extremely quiet midday trade as players sat on their hands, awaiting a key meeting of Federal Reserve policy makers on Tuesday. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 107-22/32, down 2/32 from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.06 percent.
JAPAN - The Japanese Government Bond market was closed due to a national holiday. The market will resume on September 24. On Friday the December future on LIFFE was trading at 122.10.

EUROBONDS - The primary market slowed on afternoon amid the holiday in Japan and ahead of Tuesday's FOMC meeting. In the active mark sector, among others Allgemeine Deutsche set a 200 million mark four-year FRN. The Czech Republic's Komercni Banka will price its debut mark bond this week. Colombia's mark bond, expected to be launched this week, has been delayed one week. Earlier, Lloyds TSB launched two sterling bonds totalling 250 million stg, a fixed-rate 15-year bond and a 10-year FRN. Other activity spanned French francs, guilders, lire and New Zealand dollars.
